title: Adherence to risk-tailored antiemetic prophylaxis and rescue treatment for nausea and vomiting after day surgery: a case-control study
abstract: Objective: to estimate the association between under-prophylaxis relative to a risk-tailored protocol and rescue treatment or delayed discharge for nausea and vomiting after day surgery. Design: case-control study with two controls per case from the same operating lists, using scanned anaesthetic records. Results and conclusions will be written after analysis.
introduction: Risk-tailored prophylaxis reduces nausea in high-risk patients when it is followed, but adherence is often about half, and extra agents can sedate patients.
methods: Cases from the recovery nausea log, list-matched controls, exposure classified from the drug section, conditional logistic regression adjusted for risk score, duration and opioid dose.
results: No data have been analysed yet. The report will present case and control characteristics, adherence among controls, and adjusted odds ratios for under- and over-prophylaxis.
discussion: The discussion will consider confounding by indication, case under-ascertainment, and whether adherence support should be the next improvement target.
limitations: Observational design; incomplete case capture; one unit.
summary: STROBE draft with results left empty.
